task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-06-19, in the area of play-type labeling and data quality):
Opponent next-possession PPP after you run play X is large enough to drive AVOID labels; own-sequence lags similarly matter.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: opponent next-possession PPP after own play type
methodological_questions: Is the shift in opponent next-possession PPP after you run play X large enough to change AVOID labels once it is separated from the outcome of play X, defense quality and possession-start type?
Do lags of your own previous play types or outcomes add predictive information about PPP beyond the current play type's baseline?
How do we avoid mechanical dependence, where the result of possession T determines the start type of possession T+1?
How do we control multiplicity across play types, lags and players or teams?

historical_evidence.finding: Tested opponent action T -> your offense T+1 with defense-matched 8x8 cells. 3 of 64 cells survived both matchings: SPOT_UP->TRANSITION ATT=-0.085, POST_UP->TRANSITION -0.083, PNR->DRIVE -0.058, all also surviving a prev_made control. Most of the 64 cells were null. PULL_UP->DRIVE was dropped as a defense-quality confound. Validation was recorded as same-pipeline, with BH-FDR, placebo and free-throw cleaning.

Star-level analysis of how the opponent's preceding play type affects each star's next-possession PPP. PUTBACK was the top suppressor for 6+ stars (e.g. D. Mitchell 1.178 to 0.884, d=-0.294, n_after=95). [prior work] notes no multiplicity correction, n_after of 32-95 against thousands of baseline possessions, and no validation. Its auto-assigned risk is drift/nonstationarity.

Superstar suppression profiles including Q5c sequential triggering. The rank-1 suppressor varies across players (e.g. Jokic after opp POST_UP -0.0675, SE 0.0500, n=480). Rank-1 deltas were mostly within 1-2 SE with no multiple-comparison control, and an OTHER artifact was flagged.

Observed on-ball defensive scheme labels from NBA matchup/PBP fields (ORL-DET G1). Only 14.9% (DET) and 3.3% (ORL) of possessions received a confident label, and switches_on was not populated. The verdict was failed_gate, with label error and small sample as the limitations.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Ranking per-star top suppressors from sequential play-type cells without multiplicity correction
failed_approaches.why: Small n_after (32-95) against large baselines and no multiplicity control; the failure mechanism is recorded as unclear.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Rank-1 sequential suppressor profiles per player
failed_approaches.why: Deltas were within 1-2 SE with no multiple-comparison control, and an OTHER-category artifact was flagged.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labeling on-ball coverage from NBA matchup/PBP fields
failed_approaches.why: Very low confident-label rates and an unpopulated switches_on field made the question unanswerable with this data.
It was a defense-quality confound and was dropped after matching.

evidence_establishes: Per [prior work][prior work], with defense and offense matching and FDR control, only a small minority of sequential play-type cells (3/64) show a robust next-possession effect, and those effects are about -0.06 to -0.09 PPP.
Per [prior work][prior work] and [prior work][prior work], unadjusted, uncorrected sequential effects at the player level are noisy and have not been validated.
Per [prior work][prior work], defense quality confounds sequential effects and must be controlled.
evidence_does_not_establish: Nothing retrieved tests the direction in this question (opponent's next-possession PPP after YOU run play X); [prior work][prior work] tests the reverse direction (the opponent's play -> your next possession).
Nothing retrieved evaluates own-sequence lags (your own prior possessions) as a driver of PPP or labels.
No retrieved record defines the AVOID label or shows how sensitive it is to a sequential adjustment, so 'large enough to drive labels' has no tested threshold.
No out-of-sample or cross-pipeline validation exists for sequential effects ([prior work] is same-pipeline only; the others have none).
own_inferences: The recorded sizes (about 0.06-0.09 PPP in the few surviving cells) are probably too small to flip AVOID labels, unless the label threshold is tight or cells are small. This is inference, not a recorded result.

Opponent next-possession PPP after your play is mechanically tied to how your possession ended (made basket versus miss or turnover, which sets halfcourt versus transition starts), so any raw effect is largely outcome-derived. The AVOID label is itself built from the outcomes of the same play, which raises circularity.
Own-sequence lag effects will largely reflect lineup, game-state, and team-quality persistence unless controlled by within-team, within-game designs.
The question as posed has no threshold, so as stated it is only partly falsifiable; a pre-registered practical-significance margin is needed.
uncertainties: The AVOID label definition and threshold are not given in the task or the retrieved records.
Own-sequence lag history was not retrieved; related prior work may exist but was not returned.
The accuracy of play-type labels and possession linkage in the derived graph database is not known to me.
2025-26 playoff data are partial at the posing date (complete 2026-06-21), so the data version must be frozen.
Stationarity across 2022-23 to 2025-26 is uncertain ([prior work][prior work] flags drift risk).

historical_effect.explanation: Without history I might have designed a direct test of raw lagged PPP effects. The retrieved records changed the design toward matching on defense quality, controlling for how possession T ended, FDR control, a placebo, an equivalence margin and out-of-sample replication. They also lowered my expected effect size (3/64 survivors at about -0.06 to -0.09) and made me expect a null or small result. They do not make the question untestable, so I recommend proceeding with changes rather than stopping.

blocking_constraints.text: If AVOID labels are computed from the same possessions' outcomes, the sequential effect on labels is partly circular. The label must be frozen using data that exclude the evaluated possessions.
The start type of the opponent's possession (transition versus halfcourt) is determined by the outcome of your play, so the adjusted estimand has to condition on or stratify by it.

prior_work.summary: The reverse direction (opponent play -> your next possession) has been studied with defense-matched cells; 3/64 survive, with small effects. Player-level sequential suppression was inconclusive and lacked multiplicity control. The specific question of your play -> opponent next-possession PPP and its effect on AVOID labels, and own-sequence lags, were not retrieved.

risks.text: Defense and offense quality, lineup, pace, score margin, and clock all affect both play choice and next-possession PPP; [prior work][prior work] saw a defense-quality confound.
Possession T's result drives the opponent's possession-start type and the AVOID label, producing mechanical dependence.
The design space is play types x lags x subgroups; the retrieved star-level work had no multiplicity control.
Per-star or per-team cells have n_after around 30-100 ([prior work][prior work]), too small to move label thresholds.
After a made shot the opponent starts in a halfcourt set; after a miss or turnover they often start in transition, which is mechanical and not a play-type effect.
Play-type classification error in the derived records can add noise or bias to the sequential estimates; [prior work][prior work] shows how low label coverage can be for defensive labels.
Four seasons of rule, style and pace change can produce spurious pooled effects (flagged in [prior work][prior work]).
If the AVOID threshold or reference baseline is tuned on the same seasons used to evaluate its change, results will be optimistic.
Without a placebo (e.g. shuffled or non-adjacent possession pairs), a dependence driven by game-level confounds would look like a sequential effect.

design.estimand: For each play type X, the adjusted average difference in the opponent's immediately following possession PPP after the team runs X versus matched reference possessions, conditional on the outcome of X and on the opponent possession-start type. The label-level estimand is whether this adjustment changes the AVOID classification of X by a pre-registered margin. A secondary estimand is the incremental out-of-sample predictive value of own-sequence lags (T-1, T-2 own play types and outcomes) for the PPP of play X.
design.unit: Possession pair (own possession T with play type X, opponent possession T+1) within the same game and period; clustered by game and team-season.
design.sample: Frozen data version: NBA 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 regular season and playoffs plus 2025-26 regular season (complete since 2026-04-13). Exclude 2025-26 playoffs, which are partial before 2026-06-21, or use them only as an untouched post-registration holdout once complete. Exclude pairs that cross periods, garbage time (margin above a pre-registered cutoff), or free-throw-only sequences, and pairs where the PBP linkage is ambiguous. Restrict to play types with enough pairs for the power target.
design.power: Opponent possession PPP SD is roughly 1.0-1.1 (my estimate; verify empirically). Detecting or bounding a 0.05 PPP difference with SE of about 0.025 needs roughly 1,700-2,000 pairs per arm after matching; cells with fewer pairs are reported as underpowered, not tested. Pre-register the practical margin (about 0.05 PPP, comparable to the smallest surviving effect in [prior work][prior work], an assumption) and use equivalence testing (TOST) for nulls.
design.controls: Match or regress on: opponent defense and offense quality (rolling, leave-game-out), own-team quality, lineup/minutes of starters, score margin, period, clock, pace, home/away, season; the outcome of possession T (make[path]) and the opponent possession-start type (halfcourt[path]). Fit separate models by start type. Use a cross-fitted regression (team-season fixed effects, game-clustered SEs) plus matching as a sensitivity analysis. Freeze AVOID labels on a labelling-only season (2022-23 and 2023-24) and evaluate on 2024-25, then confirm on 2025-26 regular season. For own-sequence lags, compare nested models by out-of-sample log-loss or MSE on held-out seasons.
design.falsification: Placebo 1: pair possession T with a non-adjacent opponent possession (T+3) or a random opponent possession in the same game; expect null. Placebo 2: assign play type X from a different team's possession at the same clock and game state. Negative-control outcome: opponent PPP two possessions later. Rerun after excluding transition starts and after excluding mechanically induced pairs. If effects vanish under outcome-of-T conditioning, classify as outcome-derived artifact.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register the family of play types x lag depths (1 and 2). Control the FDR at 5% (Benjamini-Hochberg) across the whole family, with per-player or per-team subgroup analyses labelled exploratory. Report all cells, not just survivors.
design.decision_rule: Supported (label-driving) only if: (a) the adjusted effect for X exceeds the 0.05 PPP margin with a BH-adjusted CI excluding it in the discovery set, (b) it replicates in the 2025-26 regular season with the same sign and at least half the magnitude, (c) the placebo and negative-control tests are null, and (d) applying the adjustment flips the AVOID label for at least one pre-registered play type. Rejected if TOST shows the effect is within the margin in adequately powered cells. Report underpowered or confounded cells as uncertain. Own-sequence lags matter only if they improve out-of-sample error by a pre-registered relative amount over the play-type-only model.
design.data_version: Per-game NBA stats API PBP, rotation, starters, matchup and box-score files plus the derived play-type possession graph, snapshot taken before analysis and hashed. Includes 2022-23 to 2024-25 full seasons and the 2025-26 regular season (complete 2026-04-13). The 2025-26 playoffs are excluded until complete on 2026-06-21, then used only as a final holdout. The AVOID label definition and threshold must be recorded in the pre-registration.
